title: OneNote on iPhone: multimodal capture in Copilot Notebooks
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, Capture policy, licensing prerequisites and consent guidance are supported by Microsoft sources. One control note should describe the documented reach of the general Pages and Notebooks policy rather than leave that reach unconfirmed.

claims.claim: Multimodal Capture lets users transcribe audio in a session.
claims.quote: Multimodal capture enables users to transcribe audio, take images, and type notes in a single session.

claims.claim: Users can capture images in the same session.
claims.quote: Multimodal capture enables users to transcribe audio, take images, and type notes in a single session.

claims.claim: Users can type notes in the same session.
claims.quote: Multimodal capture enables users to transcribe audio, take images, and type notes in a single session.

claims.where: What's changing: iPhone and iPad steps
claims.claim: The user opens OneNote, goes to Copilot Notebooks, taps Capture on the notebook list, captures the session, taps End and chooses a notebook.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot Notebooks. On the notebook list page, tap Capture. Use Capture to transcribe the discussion, take photos, and type notes during the session. When you're done, tap End. Choose the notebook where you want to save your capture.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The storage page says Pages and Notebooks are stored in OneDrive for Business.
claims.quote: Pages and Notebooks are stored in OneDrive for Business: the same visible file system where Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files live.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The storage page says Pages and Notebooks count against the user's OneDrive storage limit.
claims.quote: Quota | Counts against user's OneDrive storage limit

claims.claim: Pages and Notebooks created before November 2025 remain in a user-owned SharePoint Embedded container.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks created before November 2025 continue to be stored in the user-owned SharePoint Embedded container. These legacy Copilot Pages and legacy Copilot Notebooks haven't moved to OneDrive for Business.

claims.claim: The admin and requirements pages still describe a shared user-owned SharePoint Embedded container.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks are stored in a user-owned SharePoint Embedded container that's also used by Loop My workspace.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing: Indirect costs
claims.claim: The admin and requirements pages say this storage counts against the organisation's SharePoint quota.
claims.quote: Storage counts toward your organization's overall SharePoint quota.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft's storage page disagrees with its admin and requirements pages about storage location and quota.
claims.quote: Storage page: 'Pages and Notebooks are stored in OneDrive for Business'. Admin page: 'Copilot Pages (.page files) and Copilot Notebooks are stored in the same user-owned SharePoint Embedded container used by Loop My workspace.'

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview retention policies configured for all SharePoint sites are enforced for all Copilot Pages and Notebooks.
claims.quote: Retention policies from Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management configured for all SharePoint sites are enforced for all Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The compliance summary says DLP rules are enforced with end-user policy tips.
claims.quote: Data Loss Prevention (DLP): Rules enforced with end-user policy tip support.

claims.claim: The compliance summary lists sensitivity labels for Copilot Pages only.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels | Available - Copilot Pages only

claims.claim: Copilot Notebooks do not have container sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Copilot Notebooks don't have container sensitivity labels because they share a container with all Copilot Pages.

claims.claim: Audio processed during Capture is deleted immediately after transcription.
claims.quote: Audio data processed during a Capture session is deleted immediately after transcription and therefore can't be used for any other purpose.

claims.claim: The saved Copilot Page contains the transcript, photos and notes.
claims.quote: Copilot creates a structured Copilot Page with your transcript, photos, notes, and key insights, and saves it in your selected notebook for you to access from any Copilot Notebooks endpoint.

claims.quote: The Capture feature is available only to commercial Microsoft 365 users with work or school (Entra ID) accounts.

claims.claim: The compliance summary lists Information Barriers as not supported.
claims.quote: Information Barriers | Not supported

claims.quote: Searched: 'Capture Copilot Notebooks actions other systems iPhone'; read Capture support article and Copilot release-notes excerpts for July 01 and October 27, 2026. They describe transcription, page generation and notebook use, not actions in other systems.

claims.quote: A Microsoft Copilot license is required to use Copilot Notebooks, and an active SharePoint or OneDrive license is required to create notebooks.

claims.claim: People with OneDrive creation disabled cannot create Copilot Pages or Notebooks regardless of this Cloud Policy setting.
claims.quote: If your organization disabled the creation of OneDrive, regardless of the setting noted here, these people in your organization can't create Copilot Pages or Copilot Notebooks.

claims.claim: The Cloud Policy overview recommends Office Apps Administrator for managing policy settings.
claims.quote: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended) | This role can manage Office apps cloud services, including policy and settings management

claims.where: controls[0].ui; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The mobile Capture control is in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center under Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Capture in Copilot Notebooks for mobile devices.
claims.quote: If you're the IT admin for your organization, you can use Capture in Copilot Notebooks for mobile devices Cloud Policy to manage this feature.

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the mobile Capture control.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Capture Copilot Notebooks Microsoft Graph PowerShell Cloud Policy API mobile setting'; read Capture, overview-cloud-policy and graph/utcm-copilot-resources, searching its complete text for Capture and enumerating all 20 resource types. None covers Capture.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document the mobile Capture policy's values or the effect of Disabled.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Capture in Copilot Notebooks for mobile devices default enabled disabled Graph policy'; read Capture, cpcn-admin-configuration and overview-cloud-policy. Capture names the setting but gives no values or Disabled behaviour.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Cloud Policy supports group targeting for its user policies.
claims.quote: On the Choose the scope page, determine whether the policy configuration applies to all users, specific groups, or to users who anonymously access documents using Office for the web.

claims.claim: The Pages and Notebooks creation control is in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center under Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote: Select Customization from the left pane. Select Policy Management. Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one. From the Choose the scope dropdown list ... In Configure Settings ... For Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the Pages and Notebooks configuration in preview applyOnce mode.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object that runs periodically in the background at a scheduled frequency to detect configuration drift in monitorOnly mode, or applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode. POST /admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors

claims.claim: The Graph configurationMonitor request uses mode applyOnce to apply a baseline once.
claims.quote: mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. Optional; defaults to monitorOnly.

claims.claim: The corresponding baseline resource type is microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks.
claims.quote: "displayName": "Copilot Pages and Notebooks", "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks", "resourceVersion": 1, "properties": { "value": "1" }

claims.claim: The copilotpagesnotebooks resource's value property disables the setting with 0.
claims.quote: value | Write | String | Allows or prevents creating and viewing Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Copilot Actions. 0 disables the setting; 1 enables the setting.

claims.claim: TCM supports these Copilot Cloud Policy settings only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: TCM operations fail for a resource whose setting is configured in any group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the least-privileged signed-in user role for Copilot resource applyOnce.
claims.quote: AI Administrator is the least-privileged role for the signed-in user for remediation and applyOnce; don't assign that user-role requirement to the service principal.

claims.claim: Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks defaults to Enabled.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks creation | Cloud Policy: Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks | Enabled

claims.claim: Disabling the creation policy prevents users from creating new Copilot Pages or Notebooks.
claims.quote: When creation is disabled, users are unable to create new Copilot Pages or Notebooks.

claims.claim: Disabling the creation policy does not delete existing Copilot Pages or Notebooks.
claims.quote: Existing Copilot Pages and Notebooks aren't deleted.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly say the general Pages and Notebooks policy governs Capture.
claims.quote: Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks check the following Cloud Policy settings: Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn does not say this setting governs Capture' in controls[1].note and its rendered counterpart with 'Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks check this Cloud Policy setting.' The admin page documents that general reach; keep the narrower question about whether disabling it removes the OneNote Capture button.

claims.claim: The Capture article says Windows policy controls will become available as the feature reaches broader availability.
claims.quote: Windows policy controls will be available as the feature reaches broader availability.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy does not make every policy setting available for every operating system.
claims.quote: Policy settings are available for devices running Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android, although not all policy settings are available for all operating systems.

claims.claim: Cloud Policy uses priority to decide conflicts when a user belongs to multiple targeted Entra groups.
claims.quote: If the user is a member of multiple Microsoft Entra groups with conflicting policy settings, priority is used to determine which policy setting is applied. The highest priority is applied, with "0" being the highest priority that you can assign.

claims.claim: A Cloud Policy change can take up to 90 minutes to be reflected when policy configurations already existed.
claims.quote: If there were existing policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 90 minutes to be reflected.

claims.claim: A Cloud Policy change can take up to 24 hours to be reflected when no policy configurations previously existed.
claims.quote: If there were no policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 24 hours to be reflected.

claims.claim: No source says existing iPhone behaviour changes without the user choosing to start Capture.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Capture in Copilot Notebooks for mobile devices default enabled disabled Graph policy' and 'Capture Copilot Notebooks actions other systems iPhone'; read roadmap, Capture article and July release-notes excerpt. iOS steps start with the user tapping Capture.
